name: Lingua Franca Nova
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.verdict: a reachable source states the stress pattern
earlier_scan.source_named: Wikipedia, 'Lingua Franca Nova', Pronunciation and spelling section (read 2026-08-31), summarizing the official elefen.org grammar rule
earlier_scan.note: Fixed stress: vowel/diphthong before the last consonant of the word; non-phonemic (constructed language).

new_statements.quote: If a word has more than one vowel, one of the vowels is stressed (pronounced more strongly). ... The basic rule is to stress the vowel that precedes the last consonant of a word: falda, integra, matematica, albatros, ranur. Adding a suffix can move the stress: matematica → matematical ... But adding the plural -s does not move the stress: un falda → du faldas, un joven → tre jovenes ... The I or U of a diphthong behaves like a consonant in this regard: abaia, ciui, bonsai, cacau. If no vowel precedes the last consonant, the first vowel is stressed: trae, fea, tio, proa, jua. [Elefen original: 'La regula fundal es ce on asentua la vocal cual presede la consonante final de un parola.']

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File check: (elefen.org, English grammar ch. 1 'Spelling and pronunciation', section 'Stress', page generated from the Vici de Elefen 2026-08-03, CC BY-SA 4.0) contains the quoted passage at the stated locator. Text as extracted: 'If a word has more than one vowel, one of the vowels is stressed (pronounced more strongly). The stressed vowels below are underlined. The basic rule is to stress the vowel that precedes the last consonant of a word: falda / integra / matematica / albatros / ranur. Adding a suffix can move the stress: matematica -> matematical.. But adding the plural -s does not move the stress: un falda -> du faldas, un joven -> tre jovenes; ambos - this special word is stressed…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the vowel immediately preceding the word's last consonant (the offglide I/U of a diphthong counts as a consonant), which yields penultimate stress in vowel-final words (falda, matematica) and final stress in consonant- or diphthong-final words (albatros, ranur, bonsai); plural -s/-es is ignored; if no vowel precedes the last consonant the first vowel is stressed (trae, tio); word-final IA/IE/IO/UA/UE/UO do not attract stress (jelosia, rituo) whereas final AE/AO/EA/EO/OA/OE/UI take stress on their first vowel (idea, coneo, produi).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress; compounds (parario, mediadia) retain the original stress of the second component.
new_statements.exceptions: Plural -s/-es does not shift stress; 'ambos' is stressed like a plural; ala, asi, agu, ami, enemi, perce, alo, oce, ura are often final-stressed and either pronunciation is acceptable; estingui, vacui have semivowel U by another rule; compounds keep second-component stress. The grammar also states Elefen is not a tonal language. Wikipedia adds that stress is not phonemic.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level rule stated on citation forms of a constructed language (prescriptive official grammar by the language's creator and chief grammarian); derivational suffixes move stress, inflectional plural does not.
new_statements.identity_note: Constructed international auxiliary language (Elefen / LFN, ISO lfn), created by C. George Boeree; the source is the language's own official prescriptive grammar, so the statement is normative rather than a description of native-speaker phonology. No dialects.

new_statements.quote: The stress in multi-syllable words falls on the vowel preceding the last consonant or consonant cluster. mArto, perfEta aprIl, mUs, perfetAr. In words that have no vowel before the last consonant, the stress falls on the first vowel. mAio, mA, tIa, rEa. There is one exception to the rule: the plural -s or -es does not change the original stress of the word. rEde, rEdes, mUs, mUses, tIo, tIos. A secondary stress in words of four or more syllables falls two vowels back from the primary stress.

new_statements.relation_note: Not in the catalog (no catalog_records). Same placement as the existing statement from the elefen.org grammar (stress the vowel preceding the last consonant), so it agrees on the rule; it adds detail the existing statement lacks: the first-vowel default for words with no vowel before the last consonant, the secondary-stress rule (two vowels back, 4+ syllables) and the plural exception. The on-disk 2004 'Grammar' page (Plural Nouns) repeats the plural point: '-s and -es do not change the original stress of the word: Gáto, Gátos, Óm, Ómes'.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the vowel that precedes the last consonant (or consonant cluster) of the word, wherever that vowel sits (mArto, aprIl, perfetAr); if no vowel precedes the last consonant, stress goes on the first vowel (mAio, tIa). Stress is thus fixed by the position of the final consonant, not counted from a word edge.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Stated: in words of four or more syllables a secondary stress falls two vowels back from the primary stress.
new_statements.exceptions: The plural suffix -s / -es does not move the stress (rEde/rEdes, mUs/mUses, tIo/tIos). Words with no vowel before the last consonant take stress on the first vowel. The page also notes the language is 'very forgiving' about pronunciation.
new_statements.identity_note: Work 0 describes Lingua Franca Nova as of 2004 in its creator's original pages (www.ship.edu/~cgboeree/); the existing statement is from the current community grammar (elefen.org, generated 2026). The stress rule is the same in both, so no dialect/variety issue arises. Work 1 (webspace.ship.edu/cgboer/lfn/) is the later relocation of the same author's site and could not be opened.

sources.note: Basic rule: stress the vowel that precedes the last consonant of the word; plural -s does not move stress; I/U of a diphthong counts as a consonant; if no vowel precedes the last consonant, stress the first vowel; final IA/IE/IO/UA/UE/UO keep stress on the vowel before the consonant, final AE/AO/EA/EO/OA/OE/UI take stress on the first vowel of the pair; a short list of words (ala, asi, agu, ami, enemi, perce, alo, oce, ura) may be final-stressed; compounds keep the stress of the second component; not a tonal language.
